subjectType.description: What kind of thing the transcript records, e.g. `interview` or `call`.

subjectId.description: The record of the conversation it transcribes — an interview's id, say. `subjectType` says what kind.

provider.description:
The transcription service that turned speech into its lines — an
entry of the `transcription-services` registry, which a contract set
extends with a registry file of its own. `none` when no service was
involved: a chat, or lines a person typed.

model.description:
The transcription service's identifier for the model that produced
its lines — e.g. `scribe_v2`. Services change the model behind the
same name, so this is what tells two transcripts made a month apart
apart. Where a service does not report a version, the model the
client requested — e.g. `standard`. Required unless `provider` is
`none`.

client.description: The software that wrote its lines, as `name/version` — a transcription client, or a chat.

allOf.description:
Payload to start a transcript. What produced it is required — the
client, the transcription service, and its model unless the service
is `none` — so every transcript says where its lines came from — and
when it started, by the client's clock. id, status, createdAt and
updatedAt are set by the server.

startedAt.description: When the conversation began, by the client's clock.
